title: African Leadership Academy Class of 2027 — Financial Aid / Scholarship
description: Two-year pre-university diploma opportunity for young African leaders. ALA states that financial aid is available to make the programme accessible to successful applicants.
eligibility: Applicants for the 2027 class must have been born on or after 1 September 2007 and demonstrate strong academic potential, leadership potential, courage, perseverance and community-mindedness.
benefits: Financial aid is assessed as part of the admissions process; support is designed to make the diploma programme accessible.
requirements: Academic school records; identification/birth information; completed ALA application; evidence relevant to the admissions and financial-aid questions. Check the current application guide for the full document list.

title: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships 2027/28
field: Development-related fields under the CSC themes
description: Fully funded UK master's scholarships for talented candidates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford UK study.
eligibility: Kenya is an eligible Commonwealth country. Applicants must satisfy the CSC eligibility rules and the requirements of their nominated UK university/course.
benefits: Commonwealth scholarships provide major study support; exact award components are set by the CSC for the scheme and award.
requirements: Eligible nationality; appropriate undergraduate degree; admission/nomination requirements; development impact focus; required application statements and supporting documents.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships 2027/28
description: Funded doctoral scholarships supporting high-quality Commonwealth candidates whose research has developmental impact in eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries.
eligibility: Candidates must meet the CSC rules, nationality requirements and doctoral admission requirements, and propose research aligned with the programme's development themes.
benefits: Funded doctoral study in the UK under the Commonwealth PhD Scholarship scheme.
requirements: Eligible nationality; appropriate academic preparation; research proposal; references and supporting documents; university/course requirements; CSC application requirements.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Cambridge 2027/28
field: Climate resilience, sustainability and eligible full-time postgraduate courses
description: Fully funded master's opportunity for talented African students committed to creating sustainable futures in Africa.
eligibility: Citizen and resident of an African country, subject to the programme exceptions, and meeting the academic requirements of the chosen Cambridge master's course.
benefits: Full tuition, living/maintenance support, visa and travel support and additional scholar support are described by Cambridge.
requirements: Apply for an eligible full-time one-year Cambridge master's course; meet course academic requirements; submit the required scholarship statement and supporting application documents.

title: KU Leuven Scholarship for Africa 2027/28
description: Scholarship for outstanding African students pursuing an eligible master's or advanced master's degree at KU Leuven.
eligibility: Eligible African nationality including Kenya; residence in an eligible African country at application; excellent academic performance; previous degree obtained outside Flanders; English proficiency as required.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for the programme plus a €4,000 scholarship allowance for the programme duration.
requirements: Complete application to an eligible master's programme; KU Leuven scholarship candidacy form; English-language evidence where required; strong academic record and motivation.

title: DAAD EPOS Scholarships 2027/28 — Development-Related Postgraduate Courses
description: DAAD EPOS supports qualified professionals from developing countries in selected postgraduate programmes in Germany. Individual course deadlines vary.
eligibility: Applicants from eligible developing countries generally need an above-average first degree and relevant professional experience; individual courses can add requirements.
benefits: DAAD lists monthly scholarship payments, insurance and travel support, with possible additional allowances depending on circumstances.
requirements: First degree in a relevant subject; generally at least two years of professional experience; strong academic performance; admission and documents required by the selected EPOS course.

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters 2027 Intake
description: A portfolio of international joint master's programmes delivered by consortia of universities in multiple countries. Many programmes offer full scholarships to top-ranked students worldwide.
eligibility: Applicants generally need a bachelor's degree or to be in the final year and graduate before the master's starts; each master's programme sets its own detailed requirements.
benefits: Depending on the programme, full scholarships can cover participation costs and contribute to travel, visa and living expenses.
requirements: Bachelor's degree/equivalent; programme-specific academic requirements; application documents; language requirements where applicable. Deadlines normally vary by programme.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at UCT — Postgraduate 2027
organization: University of Cape Town / Mastercard Foundation
field: Commerce, Engineering, Health Sciences, Humanities, Law, Science
description: Comprehensive Mastercard Foundation scholarship for eligible African students applying for an eligible postgraduate diploma, honours or coursework master's at UCT.
eligibility: African citizen; first eligible postgraduate qualification; academic talent; significant social/economic barriers; leadership potential and commitment to community impact.
benefits: UCT describes comprehensive support including tuition, accommodation, living expenses, laptop, medical aid, study visa where applicable and travel, plus mentoring and leadership development.
requirements: Submit the UCT academic application and the separate Mastercard Foundation Scholars application; meet faculty/course requirements and scholarship eligibility.

title: African Leadership University — Mastercard Foundation / Financial Aid
description: ALU provides need-based financial aid and full-ride Mastercard Foundation scholarships for deserving African students, subject to availability and programme eligibility.
eligibility: Meet ALU admission requirements and demonstrate financial need. Mastercard Foundation pathways place emphasis on talented young Africans facing financial barriers, with additional attention to young women, refugees and displaced or disabled young people.
benefits: Full-ride scholarships may cover tuition and additional financial support; exact support depends on the award.
requirements: ALU admission application; academic records/transcripts; identification; financial-need evidence and any additional scholarship documents requested by ALU.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program — Partner Institutions Open Now
description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is delivered through partner universities and organisations. Current openings and deadlines vary by partner institution.
eligibility: Requirements vary by partner. The programme supports secondary, undergraduate and master's study but does not currently provide PhD scholarships through the Scholars Program.
benefits: Support can include tuition, accommodation, books/materials, mentoring, counselling, leadership development and other scholar support; exact coverage varies by partner.
requirements: Meet the chosen partner's admission requirements, demonstrate academic potential, leadership/community commitment and relevant financial or personal circumstances required by that partner.

title: Kenya Government Scholarship — Public TVET / Higher Education Funding
description: Government funding for eligible students placed in Ministry of Education TVET institutions. The 2026/27 application window has closed; keep this listing for the next intake.
eligibility: Eligible Kenyan students placed in Ministry of Education TVET institutions and assessed under the Student-Centred Funding Model.
benefits: Government scholarship support is determined by assessed financial need; eligible TVET students can also apply for HELB funding through the HEF portal.
requirements: Official admission/placement; Kenyan citizenship; HEF application; supporting information required for means testing and funding assessment.
